original_question: Does there exist a C*-algebra that is approximately amenable but not amenable? If such C*-algebras exist, how can approximate amenability be characterized within the class of C*-algebras?
target_in_paper: Question 17 in §4.3 (Other algebras). The paper asks whether there is an approximately amenable but non-amenable C*-algebra and, if so, how approximate amenability should be characterized for C*-algebras. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/1207.4511))
correct_elements: Your draft is already extremely close to the paper’s official formulation: it captures both parts of Question 17, namely the existence problem for an approximately amenable but not amenable C*-algebra and the follow-up request for a characterization inside the class of C*-algebras. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/1207.4511))
missing_details: To be fully stand-alone, it should state the paper’s exact meaning of approximate amenability: for every Banach A-bimodule X and every continuous derivation D:A→X*, there is a net (x_i) in X* such that D(a)=lim_i(a·x_i−x_i·a) in norm for each a∈A. This is the hidden quantifier structure behind the phrase “approximately amenable.” ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/1207.4511))

It should specify that A is being viewed as a Banach algebra, and that “amenable” means Johnson amenability for Banach algebras; in the C*-algebra setting the introduction recalls that this is equivalent to nuclearity. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/1207.4511))

The nearby C*-algebra context should be made explicit: because a C*-algebra has a bounded approximate identity, Theorem 2.7 makes approximate amenability equivalent to pseudo-amenability in this class. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/1207.4511))

The scope is all C*-algebras, not just reduced or full group C*-algebras; those group C*-examples are mentioned only as motivating evidence immediately before Question 17. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/1207.4511))

If one wants the sharpest paper-faithful phrasing, the first clause can be read as asking whether approximate amenability strictly extends amenability within C*-algebras; equivalently, whether approximate amenability differs from nuclearity in the C*-world. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/1207.4511))
refined_question: Let A be a C*-algebra, regarded as a Banach algebra. Does there exist such an A that is approximately amenable in the sense that for every Banach A-bimodule X and every continuous derivation D:A→X*, there is a net (x_i)⊂X* with D(a)=lim_i(a·x_i−x_i·a) in norm for every a∈A, but A is not amenable as a Banach algebra (equivalently, not nuclear)? If such C*-algebras exist, characterize exactly which C*-algebras are approximately amenable.
equivalent_formulation: Since every C*-algebra has a bounded approximate identity, approximate amenability and pseudo-amenability coincide for C*-algebras; equivalently, is there a pseudo-amenable but not amenable C*-algebra, and if so, how are the pseudo-/approximately amenable C*-algebras characterized? ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/1207.4511))
justification: The draft clearly targets §4.3, Question 17, almost verbatim, rather than any broader neighboring problem. The only real gap is that the draft is not fully self-contained: it omits the Definition 1.2 quantifiers for approximate amenability and the immediate local context that, for C*-algebras, approximate amenability coincides with pseudo-amenability, while amenability coincides with nuclearity. The refined version adds exactly those paper-critical details and does not broaden the scope beyond the stated open problem. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/1207.4511))
